bsharzbrocken.name: Brocken
bsharzbrocken.slogan: Northern Germany's highest summit, wrapped in witch-haunted mist.
bsharzbrocken.line: Fog shrouds the Brocken up to 300 days a year, and in 1958 it hit a German record of 330.

bsharzquedmarkt.name: Quedlinburg Old Town
bsharzquedmarkt.slogan: Two thousand timber houses and a castle hill, all in one lap.
bsharzquedmarkt.line: Its Ständerbau dates from 1347, one of the oldest timber-framed houses in Germany; the old town joined UNESCO in 1994.

bsgoskaiserpfalz.name: Imperial Palace of Goslar
bsgoskaiserpfalz.slogan: Where emperors held court beneath the Harz hills.
bsgoskaiserpfalz.line: Henry II built the first imperial mansion here in 1005; the 54-metre Kaiserhaus was restored between 1868 and 1879.

bsautostadt.name: Autostadt
bsautostadt.slogan: Two glass silos stacked with brand-new cars.
bsautostadt.line: Its two glass car towers are 60 metres tall, and the site draws about 2 million visitors a year.

bsburg.name: Brunswick Lion
bsburg.slogan: The bronze lion that Henry the Lion left guarding his city.
bsburg.line: Cast between 1164 and 1176, it is the first large freestanding sculpture of the Middle Ages north of the Alps.
